this is how ai digital products are scaling to $10k/mo with slideshows.

you'll need to spend 4-6 hours on this on one day. after that you've got content for 2+ months without touching it again.

the format to copy is this: content, content, content, content, ad warmup, app push.

the idea is to make slideshow posts that feel like actual content, then only bring in the product shoutout near the end.

instead of posting obvious ads, the account posts stuff that looks like normal tiktok slideshow content.

the images on this post are an example.

find hundreds of lifestyle, travel, and interior-style visuals on pinterest and google.

use ai to generate dozens of similar captions that say the same thing in different ways. sneak the product into the content without making it look promotional. post across multiple tiktok accounts.

the workflow runs on three tools:

> claude code.

> socialclaw.

> an image api. openai, gemini, or any other good image model.

here's how:

- first hour is competitor research. if your product is a health 1 search "health" on tiktok and view every top post. screenshot all of them. keep notes on what they write in captions and text over slides.

- hours two and three are reference collection. go to pinterest with those screenshots. find similar reference images. figure out what slide one should look like, what slide two should look like, and so on. download a few images for each slide type and name them slide_1_1.jpg so claude code can work with them later.

- hour four is where ai takes over. not all pinterest photos can be reposted, so ask claude code to look at the images and use the openai image api to generate 100 variations of each with slight differences but the same vibe. five slide types times 100 variations gives you 500 images. start with less if you want.

- hour five is caption generation and assembly. remember those competitor captions you saved? give them to claude and tell it "here's how the captions for our posts should look" and paste the list. claude code then comes up with slideshow angles, writes the slide-by-slide text, keeps the early slides content-first, and adds the product mention only in the later slides. claude can actually overlay text directly onto images using ffmpeg.

then ask claude to schedule two posts a day per account. socialclaw handles the upload, account management, scheduling, and publishing from there.

that's it. you're done. months of content, all scheduled.

the reason this works is that the strategy is insanely repetitive and the numbers game is in your favor.

ten accounts posting twice a day is 20 posts daily. 90% of posts land under 5,000 views, most staying under 300. but a few posts on each account hit 50k to 500k views, some crossing 1m. the format stays identical, just fresh variations of the same visual style. 0.1-2% of viewers actually visit the product page depending on your content quality. multiply that by 30 days across ten accounts and you get plenty of traffic.

once the workflow is set up, this runs like a system instead of random one-off posts.

Not Everything is For Everyone, and that's a Good Thing

The AI good, AI bad debate.
The "people don't read books anymore" panic.
The "Education isn't teaching practical skills" outrage.

The ongoing discontent in these tangential spaces boil down to one core sentiment:

"This good thing, that undeniably is good for society, should be instilled in everyone."

And, consequently,

"Because not everyone possesses, appreciates, or actively partakes this undeniably good thing for society, our civilization is in crisis."

We see this in the explosion of comments too frequently echoed: 
"AI is essential for those who couldn't to finally create art!"
"A post-literacy culture will create a dangerous bifurcation of literati vs the illiterate!"
"Education is not preparing the next generation for jobs and survival!"

I particularly do not understand it when it is the anti-communist, freedom-loving, personal-responsibility touting conservatives that clutch their pearls and gasp in such like fashion.

We have gone from "Of course everyone needs to go to college," realizing that that path doesn't work, promoting alternatives like entrepreneurship and trade skills, to now coming full circle again ---

"Of course everyone should A, B, C!"

Because the thought, once more, since no lesson has been learned, is that an elevated civilization means everyone is intelligent, productive, resourceful, driven ... in THIS particular way, or else DOOM.

I propose that an elevated civilization truly only  needs these basic elements:

1.Accountability Culture.
2.Desire to Strive for Personal Betterment.
3. Looking Up to Godliness.

Foster these, and the rest will take care of itself, in whatever form it will look like, in however it needs to look like.

That extra lift of limit on Grok Imagine?
The beautiful library of physical books?
That state-funded mandatory Home economics class?

Bells and Whistles.

The truth is, America is over-abundant -- everything can be obtained, to a degree of manner, for free, for cheap, and nigh on instantly.

The ones that are creating art, that are sitting brooding over dense great books, the ones that are solving problems... They've been doing it long before it was convenient.

The ones who haven't done so, will not even with a magic spoon.

And those in between? They are doing their thing, in ways unconventional and unfamiliar. 

We need to rein back on the obsession over Democratizing everything under the sun. Not everything is for everyone, and that is a good thing.

🔥 New open-weight vision model unifies a fragmented computer-vision landscape.

🎯 You now have one model to rule them all, or at least a shocking amount of it.

👁️ SenseNova-Vision-7B-MoT uses one instruction-following model for tasks that traditionally require separate specialist systems:

🤯 The breakthrough is breadth. 👉 Natural language selects the visual task, and one 7B-class model generates boxes, points, masks, depth maps, surface normals, or camera data through a shared interface.

📦 Object detection and localization
🔤 OCR and document understanding
🎭 Semantic, referring and interactive segmentation
📏 Depth estimation
🧭 Surface-normal prediction
🦴 Human and animal keypoints
🖥️ GUI grounding
🌐 Multi-view 3D reconstruction
📷 Camera-pose estimation
🎨 Image understanding and generation

🧠 Instead of using a separate AI model or specialized component for each vision task, SenseNova handles them all through one system.  It can return results as:
📝 Text, labels, coordinates, or bounding boxes
🖼️ Images such as masks, depth maps, or surface maps
🔀 A combination of text and visual outputs

🏆 It delivers particularly strong results against other general-purpose vision models in object detection, dense-object localization, OCR localization, and keypoints.

🔓 The code is Apache 2.0, but the released weights use CC BY-NC 4.0, meaning they are downloadable and modifiable for research and noncommercial use—not unrestricted commercial open source.

This may be an early glimpse of computer vision’s foundation-model moment: fewer disconnected tools, one programmable visual intelligence.

A New Generation Powerhouse Bringing Thai Soft Power to the Global Stage
The success of Becky Armstrong is not measured by the number of followers she has, but by her ability to serve as a bridge that introduces the beauty and charm of Thailand to the world.
Rebecca Patricia Armstrong is one of Thailand's leading actresses to have made a significant impact on the international stage through the global Girls' Love (GL) phenomenon. She also made history as the first Thai to be included in the BoF 500, the fashion industry's prestigious list of the world's most influential figures.
Most recently, she was named one of the three recipients of the Rising Star of the Year award at the 2026 Global OTT Awards in Busan for her portrayal of Nanno in the Thai fantasy thriller Girl from Nowhere: The Reset. Looking ahead, she is set to embark on a concert tour spanning more than ten countries next year, fulfilling her dream of becoming a full-fledged solo artist.
Her growing influence as a representative of a new generation of Thai cultural ambassadors has earned her recognition as one of Tatler's Gen.T Leaders of Tomorrow 2026. Yet despite achieving milestones many aspire to, the 23-year-old defines success in remarkably simple terms:
"Success, for me, is waking up every day and getting to do what I love. Having passion, being happy, wanting to meet people, and being excited to try new things."

Synthetic SFT data gets messy fast. This repo adds a graph.

GraphGen is a framework for knowledge-graph-guided synthetic data generation for LLM training and evaluation.

It helps you turn source material into targeted QA and benchmark data by first building a fine-grained knowledge graph, finding model knowledge gaps with expected calibration error, then using multi-hop sampling and style-controlled generation.

Key features:

• Knowledge-graph-guided generation – constructs a fine-grained graph from source text before creating synthetic data
• Gap-aware targeting – uses expected calibration error to identify LLM knowledge gaps and prioritize long-tail QA pairs
• Multi-hop sampling – pulls relational context from graph neighborhoods for more complex examples
• Flexible data support – supports files, databases/search sources, knowledge graphs, text/image modalities, and several output data types
• Practical run paths – includes a Gradio demo, PyPI CLI, source setup, Docker path, and downstream finetuning notes

It’s open-source (Apache License 2.0 license).

A paper worth knowing about if you're into quant trading and generative AI:

TRADES: Generating Realistic Market Simulations with Diffusion Models

Authors: Berti, Prenkaj, Velardi (Sapienza University of Rome + TU Munich)

What's inside:
> A transformer-based diffusion model for generating orders in the Limit Order Book (LOB) - realistic simulation of the market order book
> Two key metrics - realism (how close it is to real market behavior) and responsiveness (how the market reacts to an agent's actions)
> Results: ×3.27 and ×3.48 improvement over SoTA on the predictive score across two stocks
> DeepMarket - the first open-source Python framework for deep-learning-based LOB simulations
> Comes with a synthetic LOB dataset generated by the model itself

A step toward backtesting trading strategies and training RL agents on data that behaves like a real market instead of random noise.

What if your robot could remember past experiences to generate perfectly tailored training data? 

Researchers from Zhejiang Sci-Tech University and Nanjing University present EMCES: a system that uses episodic memory to guide a diffusion model, creating high-quality synthetic data for reinforcement learning. It prioritizes the most useful past moments. 

The result? Outperforms existing methods across multiple environments, boosting RL algorithm performance. 

Bonus: a hashing trick cuts storage by 8000x and time by 25.5x—without losing quality.

Episodic Memory-Guided Controllable Experience Synthesis for Reinforcement Learning
